description: Optional group DATA (owner decision 2026-10-05, item 3): displayed data verified against cited sources, or labelled, or removed. Generated by tools/t0/data/gen.mjs from tools/t0/data/fixes/*.mjs; every patch is asserted (expect) and carries its error class and source in the note. Method, sample, error rates and every fix with its source: docs/data-audit/AUDIT.md.

patches.find: Nearly all I Corps casualties fell in a 3-hour window July 1 -- one of the most compressed casualty periods of the battle.
patches.repl: Most I Corps casualties fell on July 1 (the day split is modelled; the Official Records give the corps total of 6,059 for the whole battle).
patches.note: unsupported-claim: OR 27/1 p.174, p.187

patches.find: Vermont Brigade casualties during double enfilade on Pickett's right and Wilcox.
patches.repl: Stannard's Vermont brigade (OR: 351 killed, wounded and missing in the battle, most of them on July 3) in its flank fire on Pickett's column and then on Wilcox's and Lang's brigades.
patches.note: unsupported-detail: OR 27/1 p.174 (page image: Third Brigade total 351), p.350

patches.find: Nearly ALL III Corps casualties fell in approximately 2 hours -- one of the most compressed casualty periods of the battle. Sickles's unauthorized advance created this vulnerability.
patches.repl: Nearly all of the III Corps' 4,211 casualties fell on the afternoon and evening of July 2, from about 4 p.m. until dusk. Whether Sickles's advance was authorized is disputed (Meade's report says he did not fully apprehend his instructions).
patches.note: contested-fact: OR 27/1 p.116, p.187

patches.find: "Brickyard disaster"
patches.repl: "Brickyard and the north of the town"
patches.note: unsupported-claim: OR 27/1 p.183, p.729

patches.find: Culp's Hill July 3 morning -- 7-hour fight to recapture Confederate-occupied works
patches.repl: Culp's Hill July 3 morning -- the fight to retake the works the Confederates had occupied
patches.note: unsupported-claim: OR 27/1 p.847

patches.find: Culp's Hill morning fight -- 7 hours of combat to hold captured Union works
patches.repl: Culp's Hill morning fight -- Johnson's attempt to hold the Union works he had occupied
patches.note: unsupported-claim: OR 27/1 p.847

patches.find: Steuart's brigade suffered 42.5% casualties across all three days -- highest in Johnson's division.
patches.repl: Steuart's brigade was one of the hardest hit in Johnson's division (the percentage once shown here is not supported by a source read).
patches.note: unsupported-number: OR 27/2 p.341 (return, Steuart's brigade rows)

patches.find: 26th NC (Pettigrew's brigade) suffered 588 casualties across Days 1 and 3 combined -- highest Confederate regimental total.
patches.repl: 26th NC (Pettigrew's brigade): 588 killed and wounded of over 800 engaged, most of them on July 1 (Fox), with about 120 more missing.
patches.note: wrong-claim: Fox p.555; ledger WSD-13

patches.find: Pickett's division alone suffered ~2,700 casualties -- 49% of its strength -- in approximately 30 minutes of close combat.
patches.repl: The Confederate return counts 2,888 casualties in Pickett's division, 1,499 of them captured or missing, nearly all in the assault of July 3 (OR 27/2 p.339); its strength is not given in the returns.
patches.note: wrong-number: OR 27/2 p.339 (page image: Pickett's division 232 / 1,157 / 1,499 = 2,888)

patches.find: "total_casualties": 583,
patches.repl: "total_casualties": 483,
patches.note: sum-mismatch: the file's own period figure; the Confederate returns report cavalry only for June 9 to August 1 (OR 27/2 p.334-335), so the figure is the file's (cited to Busey and Martin) and not re-verified here

patches.find: "overall_rate": 6.1,
patches.repl: "overall_rate": 5.1,
patches.note: sum-mismatch: 483 / 9,536

patches.find: Nearly 4,200 casualties in approximately 2 hours on July 2 afternoon -- the most compressed major corps casualty period of the battle.
patches.repl: The III Corps lost 4,211 killed, wounded and missing on the afternoon and evening of July 2 (Official Records).
patches.note: unsupported-claim: OR 27/1 p.187

patches.find: Approximately 2,700 casualties in 30 minutes during Pickett's Charge -- the most intense 30-minute casualty period of the battle.
patches.repl: The Confederate return counts 2,888 casualties in Pickett's division, 1,499 of them captured or missing, in the assault of July 3.
patches.note: wrong-number: OR 27/2 p.339

patches.find: Seven hours of continuous fighting July 3 morning -- the longest sustained infantry combat of the battle.
patches.repl: Kane reports fire of unintermitting strength for seven hours on the morning of July 3, from about 3:30 to about 10:30 a.m.
patches.note: unsupported-claim: OR 27/1 p.847 (Kane)

patches.repl: The totals follow the Official Records (Union corps) and Busey & Martin (the rest); the shape of each decline within a day is a model, a smooth drop around a peak tick, not a record, and the Union total shown omits the Artillery Reserve and headquarters.

patches.find: Lee wanted Lieutenant General James Longstreet's First Corps to attack the Union left early on July 2. Longstreet, who had argued against the whole offensive and preferred a defensive maneuver around the Union flank, did not get his divisions into attack position until roughly 4:00pm, hours later than Lee intended.
patches.repl: Lee ordered Lieutenant General James Longstreet's First Corps to attack the Union left on July 2 (by one account the orders went out about 11:00am, not at dawn as is often said). Longstreet, with two divisions up, waited for Law's brigade to rejoin about noon, and McLaws did not get into position until about 4:00pm; postwar accounts add that he had argued for a maneuver around the Union flank instead.
